findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the instance user_data script, which is visible to anyone with API/console access to the instance metadata or Terraform state, risking credential theft and misuse.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, meaning data at rest on this volume is stored unencrypted, exposing it to unauthorized access if the underlying storage is compromised.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume and has no encryption configured, so the snapshot data (and any copies/shares) remains unencrypted at rest.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance's management interface to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks.

The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0. While this may be intentional for a public web server, combined with the unrestricted egress and SSH rule it broadens the attack surface with no compensating controls (e.g., WAF, IP restriction).
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to instances in this subnet, increasing exposure to direct internet access when combined with the permissive security group.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to instances launched in this subnet, expanding the network attack surface unnecessarily.

The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration (aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration), leaving potentially sensitive network traffic logs unencrypted at rest.

findings.issue_category: missing public access block / bucket policy
findings.description: No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or bucket policy is defined to prevent public access to the flow logs bucket, risking accidental exposure of network traffic data.
